To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 5′ nontranslatable region of HCV is a key regulatory region that is critical for the replication of the virus.
the substitutions in the HCV 5′ NTR selected during passage of virus in lymphoblastoid (but not other) cells enhance IRES-directed translation of a reporter RNA in the same cell lines.

three substitutions in the hepatitis C virus 5′ nontranscribed region (5′NCR) that were selected for during passage of virus in lymphoblastoid (L) cells increased translation in L cells by 2 to 2.4-fold but had no effect on translation in other cell types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genetic determinants of the HCV IRES that are responsible for its cell type-specific translational activity.
the identification of genetic determinants that influence the replication efficiency of HCV.
the role of 5′NTER substitutions in HCV replication in cultured cells and suggests that the HCV IRES is cell type dependent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCV variants with substitutions within the 5′ NTR are more efficiently translated in lymphoblastoid than in hepatoma or monocytic cells.
the substitutions in the IRES of the lymphoblastoidspecific quasispecies of HCV are not sufficient to account for the increased replication in this cell type.

these 3 mutations in the 5′ NTR of HCV are not required for efficient translation of the HCV genome in lymphoblastoid and hepatoma cells but may enhance translation efficiency of the HCV IRES in lymphoblasts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three nucleotide substitutions in the IRES sequence of the HCV genome, which have been selected in lymphoblastoid (Bjab) cells, enhance translation of viral RNA in this cell line.
the three nucleotide substitutions in the HCV 5′NCR that are selected during replication in lymphoblastoid Huh-7 cells increase the translation efficiency of the viral IRES.

we have identified three nucleotide substitutions in the 5′ NTR of HCV that enhance translation efficiency of the IRES in certain human lymphoblast cell lines but not in others or in cell-free assays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a significant difference in the translation of HCV RNA by different cell lines and that this difference is due to the 5′ NTR of the HCV genome.
HCV is a very complex virus.
the 3 substitutions in the 5′ NTR that we found to enhance HCV translation in lymphoblastoid and hepatocyte cells do not appear to be selected for by the liver environment.
